# ts23d — TypeScript to 3D

> @developerz.ai/ts23d (TypeScript to 3D) — a free, deterministic 3D asset generator driven by coding agents. Assets are TypeScript modules (never JSON) built with a DSL: `defineAsset({ name, kind, real, sources, budget, build(ctx) })`, where `build` adds named, pivoted, animatable parts from primitives (`box`, `lathe`, `cylinder`, `prism`, `beam`, `planar`) or from SVG drawings written as text (`extrudeSvg`, `latheSvg`, `visualHull` front/side silhouettes), places detail with `place`/`merge`, composes other assets with `ctx.use`, and gates detail on `ctx.lod`. It compiles to glTF/GLB for any engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, three.js, Babylon) — ts23d generates assets only, the engine is yours — (3 LODs, one shared trim-sheet material, baked motion), fails a QA gate on floating parts, budget overruns and wrong real-world proportions, and renders a zero-GPU six-view contact-sheet PNG so a vision-capable agent can check its own work. The CLI needs Bun; the library imports under Node ≥ 22. Zero runtime dependencies, MIT. Status 0.x: anything unbuilt throws T3D_NOT_IMPLEMENTED with the roadmap slice that builds it. Optional tier: any model or tool through a `NeuralAdapter` (no GPU? `kubeezAdapter` for images, a partner); outputs are cached inputs, so builds stay deterministic without them.

## Offline (inside your project)
The npm package ships the docs, skills, recipe sources and examples, versioned with the code — read them without internet (As of 2026-11: recipe `out/` renders, PNGs, tests and source maps are not in the tarball; read those on GitHub):
- `node_modules/@developerz.ai/ts23d/CLAUDE.md` — rules and the loop (the repo's `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to it and is not shipped)
- `node_modules/@developerz.ai/ts23d/docs/` — DSL, IR, materials, agent loop, QA, kinds, decisions, roadmap
- `node_modules/@developerz.ai/ts23d/recipes/<name>/` — idiomatic recipes, each with its research dossier (`README.md`); committed hero + contact sheet live in the GitHub repo under `recipes/<name>/out/`
- `node_modules/@developerz.ai/ts23d/.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` — the recipe loop (`author-recipe`) and the artist workflows (`creature-artist`, `character-artist`, `hard-surface-artist`, `architect`, `prop-artist`, `rigger-animator`, `technical-artist`, …); plain markdown: read them in place or copy them into your agent's skills folder

## For agents: the loop in ten lines
The CLI with `--json` is the baseline interface (one envelope on stdout; every error a `T3D_*` code + `fix`). `t3d mcp` is an optional stdio MCP server with the same steps as tools, renders returned as images.
1. Write `assets/<name>.ts` exporting `defineAsset({...})` (real sizes in metres, Z up, +X front).
2. `bunx -p @developerz.ai/ts23d t3d build assets/<name>.ts --json` (MCP `build`) — QA verdict, findings with `fix`.
3. Fix every finding (`explain_error` / docs/architecture/errors.md for a code); rebuild until QA PASS.
4. `bunx -p @developerz.ai/ts23d t3d shot …` (MCP `shot`) — READ `out/<name>/sheet.png`; name the single worst error.
5. Fix it, rebuild. `t3d hero` / `t3d blueprint` (MCP `hero`, `blueprint`) for the textured look and measures.
6. `t3d review` (MCP `review`) — read `review/*.png`, follow `review.md`.
7. `t3d critique` (MCP `critique`) — calibrated score pack; never score above what the renders show.
8. Add LOD-gated detail, weather, repeat from 2.
9. Stop when two looks in a row find nothing worth fixing.
10. MCP setup (optional): `claude mcp add ts23d -- bunx -p @developerz.ai/ts23d t3d mcp` (any MCP client: command `bunx`, args `-p @developerz.ai/ts23d t3d mcp`, run in the project root). Tools only touch the project root and `--out`.

## The workflow
The human names a thing ("Tiger I, mid-production 1943"). The agent researches specs and real photos into `recipes/<name>/README.md` (every number sourced), writes `recipes/<name>/<name>.ts` (in your project: `assets/<name>.ts`) with `sources` + `real.measures` from that dossier, compiles until QA PASS (budget, surface contact, clashes, proportions ±5%, measures ±2%), renders the six-view contact sheet, looks at it, adds LOD-gated detail, and iterates.

## Programmatic (no CLI)
`t3d` is optional: `compile` → `runQa` → `toGlb` / `contactSheet` / `paintTrimSheet` are plain functions returning bytes. Runnable script: `examples/build-with-bun.ts` (also in the npm package).
- [Tuning](docs/idea/20-tuning.md): `t3d tune <recipe> [--evals N] [--seed s]` fits `tune.params` (read with `ctx.tuned`) to silhouette/measures/art/budget objectives by CMA-ES offline and writes `tune.json`, `tune-report.md`, `tune-strip.png`; builds read the committed numbers.
- Faces: `recipes/_lib/face` warps a committed CC0 base head (MakeHuman hm08, pinned) to ~40 code-set landmarks with `warpTPS` / `tpsWarp` (thin-plate spline, `@developerz.ai/ts23d/primitives`); race presets (human, orc, elf, dwarf, goblin) are numbers. Demo `recipes/face_demo`: the code is the brain, the base mesh is the face.
- [Import](docs/idea/21-import.md): `importGlb(source, opts)` (reader bounds and caps; shipped) brings a licence-pinned GLB (scan, CC0 base mesh) in as a part: cleaned, axis-fixed, `simplify` per LOD (ADR 011), `bakeNormals`, one trim-sheet material by default. Demo `recipes/import_demo`.
- [AI finish](docs/idea/22-ai-finish.md): `t3d finish <recipe> --endpoint URL --prompt "…"` projects model-painted views onto LOD0 as one texture layer, masked per part; geometry, names and motion unchanged; QA for palette drift and mask leaks. Demo `recipes/finish_demo`.
- [Real data](docs/idea/23-real-data.md): `@developerz.ai/ts23d/data` — `bun run data wikidata <QID>` → `realFrom`, `bun run data dem --centre lat,lon --size m` → `terrainFromDEM`; offline builds, sha256-pinned. Demo `recipes/real_valley`.

## Reference
- [Public API barrel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/src/index.ts)
- [Error codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/docs/architecture/errors.md): every T3D_* with cause and fix
- [Module tiers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/docs/architecture/README.md)
- [glTF capabilities](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/docs/architecture/gltf-capabilities.md): every extension, skins, physics drafts; what ts23d writes
- [Roadmap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/docs/plans/roadmap.md): shipped vs planned
- [Releases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/docs/changelog/README.md): every version with its one-sentence summary, a page each (changes, diff, npm link); full log in CHANGELOG.md
- [Decisions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/docs/decisions/): why TS not JSON, why one material, why CPU renders
- [Example recipe: Tiger I](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/recipes/tiger_1/tiger_1.ts)
- [Reference dossier template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/ts23d/main/recipes/README.md)

- Parts kit: search recipes/_parts/README.md before writing geometry; definePart (docs/idea/14-parts.md).

- Playbooks: docs/playbooks/README.md — class-by-class guidance (vehicles, buildings, props, nature, characters) from a name to sourced specs, part tree, motion, QA.
- Art as text: docs/idea/16-art-as-text.md — art principles as measurable definitions, DSL words and checks.

- Lettering: `text(str, { font })` — 5 × 7 pixel (`'5x7'`, `'block'`, Latin + Cyrillic) or smooth Hershey stroke faces `'sans'`, `'serif'`, `'script'`, `'gothic'` (ASCII) with `weight`, `segments` (pick from `ctx.lod`), `cap`, kerning; flush or raised `depth`; `measureText`. Specimen: `recipes/type_specimen`.

- Finishes and optics: lacquered paint (clearcoat), glass/ice/liquid/jelly (transmission, ior, volume), sheen, anisotropy, iridescence; `--profile unreal|unity|godot|rt|web` (docs/idea/02-dsl.md).

- Sound: `sound.impact|engine|mechanism|ui` (`@developerz.ai/ts23d/audio`) — deterministic WAVs from material, size, cylinders/RPM, part motion; positional `KHR_audio_emitter` (docs/idea/17-sound.md).

- Tiers (as of 2026-11): CPU tier builds byte-identical with no GPU; the optional model tier plugs any model in through `NeuralAdapter` (`t3d neural ls|run`, outputs committed under `recipes/<name>/neural/<key>/` with `record.json`; `T3D_NEURAL_MISSING` falls back to the CPU path). `t3d doctor` / `t3d setup tools|gpu-min|gpu-full` / `t3d server start|stop|status` install and check it (docs/idea/08-neural-adapters.md). Organic assets (creatures, humanoids; As of 2026-11) are model-first and Blender-first: concept image (exact side profile for a quadruped, A-pose front for a biped, flat light) -> image-to-3D mesh (local GPU Pixal3D / TRELLIS.2, or Meshy as a hosted, paid option; `keep: 'local'`) -> recipe-written `blender` steps (retopo shell, uv, bake, bind, repose, weights, lods; ops and gates in `examples/blender/README.md`) -> `importModel` -> one textured part per LOD (`TextureSet`, ADR 016; one material per set; `budget.textureSets`). Code keeps scale, skeleton, clips, budgets and QA (gate `model`: `T3D_MODEL_FIT|SKELETON|TEXTURE|DOUBLED`). Kinds: `modelChain`, `defineModelCreature`, `riggedChain`, `defineModelCharacter`. Look with `t3d blender review <recipe.ts> --out <dir>` (needs Blender; never cached); fill the cache with `t3d neural run` (paid adapters print credits; `--yes-spend` above 50; committed cache <= 12 MB per recipe). Shipped assets: `recipes/ranger` (rigged humanoid, `defineModelCharacter`) `recipes/wolf_hybrid` (quadruped, `defineModelCreature`: Pixal3D mesh, UniRig joints, walk and trot) and `recipes/bear_hybrid` (plantigrade quadruped, walk); the dragon model tier is planned. Limits: fused fingers, sculpted-clump hair, no jaw or blink on a fused head. Skills: `creature-artist`, `character-artist`.
- Realism tools: `photoMatch` + `solveCamera` + `silhouetteIoU`; `t3d critique` calibrated score (flagships near 6 of 10, target 8.5, floor not yet enforced); sculpt engine (cubic kernels, strokes, `fair()`, VDM stamps); `creature()` with bones, fur cards, `skinWeights`, glTF skins and clips (walk/trot/gallop), `skin`/`deform`/`gait` QA; `t3d hero --quality path` (CPU path tracer); `t3d finish --hero` (normal/AO/height/ORM bake); Blender, gltfpack, Basis KTX2 and Godot tool adapters.
- Game projects: `t3d init --engine godot|three|unity|unreal|babylon`, `assets/PLAN.md` + `t3d plan check`, `t3d build --watch`, `t3d concept <recipe.ts|brief.md>` (image adapter; no GPU: kubeez.com, partner, disclosed), `t3d neural run --allow-bad-input` (recorded override of the input-image rules).

- Weathering: `weather()` — seeded, geometry-driven rust streaks, chips, dust, moss, mud, bleach, dents, sag with `where` selectors and `amount` coverage measured into the manifest; QA `weather` (docs/idea/18-weathering.md).
